newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand was stronger against the dollar in quiet late Wednesday dealings but its leisurely progress over the day suggested the unit's mini recovery from last week's importer-related shock was slowing.
At 1422 GMT, the rand was at 4.4575/4605 to the dollar from Tuesday's late level of 4.4640/4670.
Dealers said turnover was thin throughout the day and any strength was due mainly to some local dollar selling and general position squaring to avoid being slugged with carry costs.

"It hasn't moved much at all. You will probably see the rand move stronger after South African trading time because every Wednesday people sell dollars because of carry and the carry's good at 60 points or so," said one dealer.
In cross rate action, the rand improved slightly and was last at 0.3798/3802 marks, up from 0.3792/3797 late Tuesday and at 25.5240/5480 yen from 25.4169/4452 before.
The unit fell against the sterling and was at 7.3433/3527 rand to the British pound from 7.3199/3293 rand previously.
The fortunes of the debt market darkened over the day as the generally long market took profits.
The benchmark R150 long bond was last at 14.955 percent from a previous 14.865 percent, having briefly flirted with the key psychological level of 15.00 percent.

Dealers said jobbers managed to push yields into the black early on the back of U.S. interest rate inaction from the FOMC but some additional supply, rumoured to have come from the Reserve Bank prompted banks to take profits around 14.82 percent.

The upward momentum was arrested around 14.92 percent over midday and into the afternoon by some of the same banks picking up the now cheaper long bond, but the ceiling didn't hold and bonds staggered yet weaker in late trade.
Foreigners were net sellers of 38.79 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after selling 596.73 million rand's worth on Monday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal Bond Exchange turnover slipped to 5.47 billion rand on Tuesday from 6.24 billion rand Monday.
South Africa's money market shortage was barely changed on Tuesday at 6.658 billion rand from Monday's level of 6.556 billion rand, the Reserve Bank said on Wednesday.

Domestic short term money market rates were a jot lower compared to Tuesday with three month NCD rates from major banks lining up at 16.35 percent from a range of 16.35 percent to 16.40 percent offered on Monday, while 90-day BA rates remained at 15.90 percent.
Money market dealers said there was likely to be little impact from the massive funds inflow -- expected to begin on Thursday -- stemming from the part privatisation of communications utility Telkom.
